paper_title: AttentionInfluence Adopting Attention Head Influence for Weak-to-Strong   Pretraining Data Selection
caption: The statistics of clustering. The left is the clustering result of AttentionInfluence, the right part is that of FineWeb-Edu Classifier.
model_annotation: The two pie charts compare the distribution of categories between "AttentionInfluence" and "FineWeb-Edu Classifier". The "AttentionInfluence" chart has 16 slices, with the largest being "Education" (25%, blue), followed by "History & Society" (23%, orange), and "Health & Medicine" (22%, blue); other notable categories include "Animal & Plant" (13%, red), "Tech & Engineer" (12%, red), "Society & culture" (10%, orange), "Teaching & resources" (15%, green), and "Science & technology education" (10%, green), with the remaining categories ranging from approximately 1-7%. The "FineWeb-Edu Classifier" chart also has 16 slices, with the largest being "Education" (38%, blue), followed by "Science & technology education" (19%, green), and "History & Society" (19%, orange); other notable categories include "Health & Medicine" (19%, blue), "Teaching & resources" (17%, green), and "Science" (15%, blue). Both charts display category labels and numerical values inside or adjacent to each slice, with no legends or visually emphasized slices. The slices in both charts are generally arranged in a clockwise order by size, with the largest slices first.
